title: How can one table of ten numbers be filled quickly?
description: Ten numbers are tested for two, three, four, five, six, eight, nine, ten and eleven. Each test looks at one part of the number, so the table is filled column by column, and three quick facts check the result.
teaching_notes: One idea: each divisibility test reads one part of the number, so a column can be filled without dividing. Watch for students who test every number by long division, or who forget that a Yes for nine needs a Yes for three.

source: Checking Divisibility Quickly: fill the table
video_script.why: A learner fills a ten by nine Yes and No table by reading one part of each number per test, and checks it with three quick facts.
video_script.anchor: the table of ten numbers against nine tests, filled column by column
video_script.payoff_line: The table is filled, and every quick fact holds.

hold_back: Divisible by (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11): 128 Y N Y N N Y N N N; 990 Y Y N Y Y N Y Y Y; 1586 Y N N N N N N N N; 275 N N N Y N N N N Y; 6686 Y N N N N N N N N; 639210 Y Y N Y Y N N Y Y; 429714 Y Y N N Y N Y N N; 2856 Y Y Y N Y Y N N N; 3060 Y Y Y Y Y N Y Y N; 406839 N Y N N N N N N N
maths_rules: 6 is Yes where 2 and 3 are both Yes: 990, 639210, 429714, 2856, 3060
last two digits for 4: 28, 56 and 60 are multiples of 4 (128, 2856, 3060); last three digits for 8: 128 and 856 are multiples of 8 (128, 2856), 060 is not
alternating signs for 11: 990 gives 0 − 9 + 9 = 0; 275 gives 5 − 7 + 2 = 0; 639210 gives 0 − 1 + 2 − 9 + 3 − 6 = −11; the rest are not multiples of 11
quick facts: a Yes for 4 or 8 needs a Yes for 2; a Yes for 9 needs a Yes for 3; 6 is Yes exactly when 2 and 3 are
video_script.design: One idea: fill the table by tests, one part of the number at a time. Assumes the shortcuts for 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. The ten numbers stay as rows and the nine tests as columns all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about ten numbers and nine tests.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>For each number and each test, we write Yes or No.
Is there a quick way to fill all ninety boxes?

narration: <bookmark mark='card'/>Each shortcut reads one part of a number.
<bookmark mark='units'/>The units digit decides two, five and ten.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last two digits decide four, and the last three digits decide eight.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The digit sum decides three and nine.
<bookmark mark='signs'/>Six needs two and three together. Eleven uses alternating signs.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Given, ten numbers. One hundred twenty eight, nine hundred ninety and one thousand five hundred eighty six.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Next, two hundred seventy five and six thousand six hundred eighty six.
Then six lakh thirty nine thousand two hundred ten.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Then four lakh twenty nine thousand seven hundred fourteen.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Then two thousand eight hundred fifty six and three thousand sixty.
Last, four lakh six thousand eight hundred thirty nine.

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write Yes or No for every test, for every number.

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step one, use the units digit. For two, every number is Yes except two numbers.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>Those are two hundred seventy five and four lakh six thousand eight hundred thirty nine.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Three numbers end in zero. They are nine hundred ninety, six lakh thirty nine thousand two hundred ten and three thousand sixty.
<bookmark mark='five'/>For five, those three are Yes, and so is two hundred seventy five, which ends in five.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>For ten, only the three numbers ending in zero are Yes.

marks.nine: column 9 is filled with Yes for the sums 18, 27 and 9

narration: <bookmark mark='sums'/>Step two, add the digits. The sums are eleven, eighteen, twenty, fourteen, twenty six, twenty one, twenty seven, twenty one, nine and thirty.
<bookmark mark='three'/>For three, the sums that are multiples of three are Yes. Eleven, twenty, fourteen and twenty six are No.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>For nine, only the sums eighteen, twenty seven and nine are Yes.
<bookmark mark='six'/>For six, we need Yes for both two and three. Five numbers have both.

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step three, look at the last digits. For four, the last two digits must make a multiple of four.
<bookmark mark='fouryes'/>That is Yes for one hundred twenty eight, two thousand eight hundred fifty six and three thousand sixty.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>For eight, the last three digits must make a multiple of eight. Three thousand sixty fails, so it is No.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>For eleven, use alternating signs. Nine hundred ninety and two hundred seventy five give zero, and the six lakh number gives minus eleven. These three are Yes.

narration: <bookmark mark='facts'/>Step four, check the table with three quick facts. A Yes for four or eight needs a Yes for two.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>A Yes for nine needs a Yes for three.
Six is Yes exactly when two and three are both Yes.
<bookmark mark='pass'/>Every row of the table passes all three.
